mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4.5% in a single month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% in a given month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-trigger mean (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 coincides with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investor sentiment deteriorates on labor market weakness.
regime_hint: Early signs of labor market softening
failure_condition: Over 10 consecutive months with PAYEMS > 200,000, the 5-day forward return is never negative (empirical probability < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) grows faster than consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over two consecutive months, it signals supply-side strength that supports higher equity valuations and positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate for months t-1 and t
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive instances where the trigger occurs, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in residential housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as capital allocation shifts from housing to equities.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During the three-month HOUST decline window, the 60-day forward return is not negative in more than 40% of observed periods (empirical probability ≤ 0.6).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market and typically precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls for two consecutive months below 4.0%
failure_condition: Over 10 such UNRATE declines, the 20-day forward return is never positive (empirical probability > 0.7).

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (not in catalog; fallback: use RSAFS as proxy for broad demand) rise faster than consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) in the prior month, it predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as demand outpaces price pressures.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate in month t-1
failure_condition: Across 20 triggered instances, the 5-day forward return is not positive in more than 70% of cases (empirical probability ≤ 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) above the prior month's level by at least 50,000 but below 200,000 is followed by a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market interprets labor market resilience.
failure_condition: In 30 such trigger events, the 20-day forward return is not positive in more than 50% (empirical probability ≤ 0.5).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 50-week moving average predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals weakening manufacturing momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months below its 50-week MA
failure_condition: During all observed 60-day windows with this trigger, the 60-day forward return is not negative in more than 30% of cases (empirical probability ≤ 0.7).
